Prime Minister shares an article highlighting India's energy transition, wider access and energy security
articles.full_content:
The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, today shared an article highlighting India’s energy story under the Prime Minister's leadership, marked by wider access, faster renewable growth and greater energy security.
The article outlines how, from electricity and clean cooking to solar, nuclear power and biofuels, India is steadily building a more diverse and robust energy system while playing a bigger role in global energy trade and technology.
The Prime Minister’s Office posted on X:
“India's energy story under PM @narendramodi is one of wider access, faster renewable growth and greater energy security. From electricity and clean cooking to solar, nuclear power and biofuels, India is steadily building a more diverse and stronger energy system. The journey is also giving India a bigger role in global energy trade and technology.”

Ministry of MSME commences “Special Campaign 6.0” to meet goals of institutionalizing Swachhata and minimizing pendency across its offices
articles.full_content:
Ministry focuses on effective e-Waste management, cleanliness, space management and disposal of pending matters
The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, has commenced the Special Campaign 6.0, being organised from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026 with the objective of institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency across its offices.
The Campaign places special emphasis on effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste , along with cleanliness, space management, beautification of office premises, disposal of scrap and redundant items, record management and disposal of pending references and other matters.
The Ministry had organised a preparatory meeting on 17th September, 2026 for sensitising about the objectives, timelines and parameters of Special Campaign 6.0 and for drawing up a coordinated action plan for the Campaign. The Ministry and its attached organisations have undertaken activities, including:
• Identification of e-Waste: Lying in premises for disposal in accordance with the prescribed guidelines.
• Cleanliness and Space Management: Cleanliness campaign sites are identified and space management, beautification of office premises, and disposal of scrap and redundant items are planned.
• Disposal of Pending Matters: Pending references, Public Grievances, Appeals and Parliamentary Assurances are being disposed.
• Target-setting and Action Plan: Nodal Officers and Divisions/Sections of the Ministry have set targets and comprehensive Action Plans for implementation of the Campaign.
The Ministry has sensitised its attached organisations to ensure coordinated implementation of the Campaign, with special emphasis on field offices responsible for service delivery and having public interface. The Ministry of MSME remains committed to carry forward the objectives of Special Campaign 6.0 through sustained efforts towards Swachhata, efficient disposal of pendency and improved workplace environment .
Hybrid meeting held with officer of M/o MSME and its organisations for prepration of Special campaign 6.0
Standees for Special Campaign 6.0 installed in M/o MSME, Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi

New metal-free porous material can help produce affordable clean energy
articles.full_content:
A breakthrough metal-free catalyst developed by scientists could significantly reduce the cost of next-generation clean-energy technologies.
In energy storage devices such as zinc–air (Zn–air) batteries, oxygen from the air reacts with the electrode in a process known as the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The efficiency with which the battery operates is determined by this reaction. Zn–air batteries are a promising option for next-generation energy storage as they utilise the abundant, inexpensive and relatively safe element zinc while drawing oxygen directly from the air, thus eliminating the need to store an active cathode material. Compared with conventional lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries, Zn–air batteries offer the potential for higher theoretical energy density, lower material cost, improved safety and greater sustainability. However, challenges related to rechargeability, cycle life and ORR kinetics remain.
Compared with hydrogen fuel cells, Zn–air batteries can provide a simpler, more compact energy storage solution that does not require high-pressure hydrogen storage or extensive hydrogen infrastructure. However, both Zn–air batteries and hydrogen fuel cells critically rely on efficient oxygen electrochemistry. Currently, many clean-energy technologies, particularly hydrogen fuel cells, depend on platinum, one of the world’s rarest and most expensive metals, as an efficient ORR catalyst. While platinum provides excellent catalytic performance, its high cost, scarcity and limited availability remain major barriers to large-scale deployment. Therefore, developing efficient, platinum-free ORR catalysts is crucial for realising the cost, sustainability and scalability advantages of Zn–air batteries, and for advancing affordable clean-energy technologies.
A team of researchers from S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences (SNBNCBS), Kolkata, and Institute of Nano Science and Technology (INST), Mohali, both institute of Department of Science and Technology (DST) as well as from SRM University, Amaravati, has now demonstrated that a specially designed metal-free organic porous material, prepared from 2,4,6-tris(4-aminophenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (TTT) and 4,8-dioxo-4,8-dihydrobenzo[1,2-b:4,5-b’]dithiophene-2,6-dicarbaldehyde (DHTD) linkers, named as TTT-DHTD. Interestingly, TTT-DHTD can perform almost as well as platinum without using any precious metals when used as the air-electrode catalyst in Zn–air batteries. This was published in the journal Science Advances.
Built entirely from abundant elements such as carbon, sulfur, nitrogen, and hydrogen, the material forms an ultra-porous, honeycomb-like network that efficiently converts oxygen into electricity—a key step in generating power in a fuel cell. Laboratory tests showed that the new catalyst achieved about 96% of the performance of commercial platinum catalysts, while remaining remarkably stable. BIS Eastern Regional Office Celebrates Manak Mahotsav 2026 with Focus on Standards for Clean Energy
articles.full_content:
World Standards Day celebration highlights role of standards in achieving SDGs
Kolkata, October 07, 2026
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Eastern Regional Office, Kolkata, celebrated Manak Mahotsav 2026 on the occasion of World Standards Day in Kolkata today. The celebration was organised on the theme “Shared Vision for a Better World – Standards for SDGs”, with a special focus on Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy.
Shri Tapas Roy, Minister-in-Charge, Department of Industry, Commerce & Enterprises; Public Enterprises & Industrial Reconstruction; and Non-Conventional & Renewable Energy Sources, Government of West Bengal; Professor S. P. Gon Chaudhuri, renowned energy expert and Dr. Meenakshi Ganesan, Deputy Director General, Eastern Region, BIS attended the event.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Roy and Professor Chaidhuri highlighted the importance of Indian Standards in promoting quality, reliability and safety in the energy sector and in supporting the transition towards affordable, clean and sustainable energy.
As part of the celebration, BIS felicitated industries and laboratories for their outstanding contribution to the standardization and quality ecosystem.
A technical session was organised with participation from experts representing Exide Industries, Schneider Electric, N. B. Institute of Rural Technology (NBIRT) and the field of climate change. The session deliberated on energy storage, clean energy transition, climate change and sustainable practices, highlighting the role of standards in facilitating a resilient and sustainable energy ecosystem.
The event also showcased various consumer-centric initiatives of BIS, including the BIS CARE App, which has crossed one crore downloads. The app enables consumers to verify BIS licences and Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) numbers, lodge complaints and locate BIS-recognized laboratories.
The celebration brought together stakeholders from industry, laboratories, academia and government departments, reaffirming the collective commitment towards quality, sustainability and effective implementation of standards. The event highlighted the crucial role of standardization in advancing the Sustainable Development Goals and building a safer, more sustainable and resilient future.

DDWS Organised Regional Review Meeting of States/UTs under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 at IIM Bangalore
articles.full_content:
Secretary, DDWS urges States to strengthen source sustainability, water quality surveillance and service delivery under JJM 2.0
The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised a regional review meeting of States and Union Territories under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM Bangalore) today. The meeting was chaired by Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, in the presence of Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), and attended by senior officials from States and UTs. The meeting reviewed the progress of JJM 2.0 and discussed key reform measures relating to source sustainability, water quality surveillance, digital governance, community participation and long-term sustainability of rural water supply systems.
In his opening address, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena emphasised that Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 marks a significant shift from infrastructure creation to sustainable and accountable service delivery. He urged States and UTs to accelerate implementation of approved schemes and effectively utilise available resources while ensuring that investments are directed towards fully functional schemes delivering reliable drinking water services to rural households. Stressing the importance of outcomes-based implementation, he underlined that expenditure must be translated into functional infrastructure supported by complete source-to-household connectivity, robust digital records and effective monitoring systems.
Secretary Shri Meena highlighted that Jal Jeevan Mission has transformed rural drinking water access across the country, with more than 15.96 crore rural households now having tap water connections compared to only 3.27 crore households at the time of the Mission's launch in August 2019. He noted that the focus of JJM 2.0 is on sustaining these gains through source sustainability, financial and operational efficiency, water quality assurance and citizen-centric service delivery.
Shri Meena called upon States to expedite implementation of both single-village and multi-village water supply schemes, particularly in quality-affected areas, and ensure timely utilisation of available resources. Referring to the decisions taken during recent sectoral deliberations on water governance, he urged States and UTs to establish effective mechanisms for monitoring and implementing agreed reform measures to further strengthen service delivery under JJM 2.0.
Highlighting findings emerging from Jal Seva Adhayan , he observed that pipeline leakages and breakages continue to be the leading cause of water supply disruptions, followed by power cuts and low-voltage related challenges. He emphasised the need for States to adopt both immediate and long-term solutions to improve the reliability of rural water supply systems and ensure uninterrupted drinking water services to rural households.

Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 : MoPR and DDWS Take Cleanliness and Waste Management Message to the Panchayats
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj actively observed Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 from 17th September to 2 nd October 2026 under the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat” . In close collaboration with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), the Ministry issued a Joint Advisory to mobilise all stakeholders, including Panchayati Raj Institutions and Rural Local Bodies, for the successful implementation of the campaign and in furtherance of the Sankalp of ‘Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’. The key focus areas of SHS-2026 were the Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) and Clean Public Places; Swachh Paathshala – Yuva for Swachhata; SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir; Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata; and Swachhata se Samriddhi. The DDWS and the Ministry of Panchayati Raj have complementary roles in mobilising rural communities for Swachhata, with Panchayati Raj Institutions playing a central part in drawing out local participation and sustaining its impact through regular sanitation activities. T he campaign sa w active involvement of the Panchayati Raj Departments of States and Union Territories, Panchayat representatives, functionaries as well as the citizens.
With the onset of the campaign, Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh and the Union Minister of State for Panchayati Raj, Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel reached out to the masses through various mediums spreading the message of the need to imbibe cleanliness as a way of life. Efforts to sensitise citizens about the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, also gathered momentum during the campaign. On Swachh Bharat Diwas, 2nd October 2026, Special Gram Sabhas were held across the country alongside the People’s Plan Campaign, Sabki Yojana SabkaVikas w herein all stakeholders were made aware about the SWM Rules, 2026, and plantation drives under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’were taken up. On this occassion, Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, participated in the cleanliness drive in Lakhisarai district of Bihar and planted a sapling, calling upon citizens to make cleanliness a part of their daily lives and to become active partners in building a clean, healthy and green India. Earlier as part of the campaign, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Shri (Dr.) Vineet Joshi, administered the Swachhata Pledge to all officers and staff while the Ministry came together for Shramdaan at a public space opposite Prachin Hanuman Mandir, Connaught Place on 1st October 2026 to not just promote cleanliness but also acknowledge the invaluable contribution of Sa fai Mitras and Safai Karamcharis in making our daily lives smoother by their contributions.

Ministry of Coal holds Special Drive with focus on E-waste Management as part of Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
In accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) regarding Special Campaign 6, Ministry of Coal has held a special drive with focus on E-Waste Management across all the coalfield offices on 6 th October, 2026. 2152 employees across 74 field offices participated in this special drive.
A one-day workshop on “E-Waste Management” chaired by Joint Secretary Shri Sanjeev Kumar Kassi, was held at the Ministry of Coal (MoC) Conference Room in hybrid mode. Ms. Riya Soni, Scientist-B, CPCB, MoEFCC, made a presentation on e-waste management, covering key aspects of responsible e-waste handling and management.
The workshop aimed to sensitize officials of the Ministry of Coal and its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) on the critical need for systematic segregation and proper disposal of electronic waste (e-waste).
This workshop was attended by Senior officials from the Ministry who attended the workshop in person, while officials from Coal India Limited (CIL) and its subsidiaries, NLC India Limited (NLCIL), Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL), Coal Controller’s Organisation (CCO), and the Coal Mines Provident Fund Organisation (CMPFO) participated virtually.
Quiz Competition at CCO:
The Coal Controller's Organization (CCO) office in Delhi organized a quiz competition on the theme of 'E-Waste Management.
In line with the overarching theme of Special Campaign 6, E-Waste Collection Workstations (E-Waste Kiosk) to facilitate systematic collection, segregation, and responsible disposal of electronic waste at the ground level were held at various field offices.

articles.title: Chintan Shivir 2026 Concludes with Focus on Collaborative Knowledge Sharing for Quality Road Infrastructure
articles.full_content:
Two-day conclave provides platform for Centre, States and stakeholders to share experiences, best practices and practical solutions
The two-day “Chintan Shivir 2026 – A National Conclave on Highway Infrastructure” concluded today at Statue of Unity, Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, with a renewed focus on strengthening Centre-State collaboration, sharing field-level experiences and building institutional capacity for delivery of quality road infrastructure.
In his valedictory address, Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Shri V. Umashankar, said the Chintan Shivir has provided an opportunity to create a common community of the highways and road sector, enabling States and other stakeholders to share initiatives, experiences and solutions at the policy as well as implementation levels.
Shri Umashankar highlighted that the focus of infrastructure development is increasingly shifting towards quality, with the vision of Viksit Bharat requiring high-quality roads across urban and rural areas, State Highways, National Highways and Expressways.
A key outcome of the deliberations was the opportunity for States to leverage technology platforms and institutional capabilities developed at the national level. Platforms such as PM GatiShakti, Data Lake, eDAR, contractor rating systems and Bhoomi Rashi can be made available for State-level applications, with technical handholding and capacity-building support.
The AI-enabled eDAR platform, currently being used for the National Highway network, can also support States in analysing accident patterns on State and local roads and developing evidence-based interventions for improving road safety, subject to availability of relevant road data.
The deliberations also highlighted the need to strengthen the construction ecosystem through professionalisation, skill development and improved supervision. Shri Umashankar emphasised the importance of focused skill development and capacity building among construction workers to enhance construction practices and ensure better quality outcomes.
Emphasis was also placed on strengthening the quality-based selection and performance assessment of DPR consultants, Authority Engineers and Independent Engineers, with greater weightage to technical capability and past performance. These measures are aimed at addressing gaps in supervision and ensuring better project outcomes.
The conclave further discussed the scope for States to adopt innovative contracting and financing mechanisms, including Model Concession Agreements, BOT and Annuity-based models, particularly for the development of State Highways and State Expressways. The experience and expertise developed at the national level can be utilised by States through structured handholding and capacity-building.
Shri Umashankar also invited States to organise their own Chintan Shivirs and workshops, with participation from domain experts and officers to facilitate knowledge exchange and wider adoption of successful practices.

FINAL COMPLETION REPORT on Kisan Sangosthi under Reform Utsav 2026-By S.KARUPPAIAH .MANAGER MARKETING TELANGANA STATE
articles.full_content:
Venue Department of Agriculture & M/s Annadatha Fertilizers, Pesticide and Seeds, Village Utlapally, Miryalaguda Mandal, Nalgonda Dist, Telangana.State
Organized by:Shri S. Karuppaiah, Manager Marketing - Telangana State, MFL RO-Hyderabad.
Field Coordination & VVIP: Shri S. Gopi, AEO, Vootlapally Cluster, Miryalaguda Mandal, Department of Agriculture, Govt. of Telangana.
Participation: Total 40 farmers from Utlapally and sorrounding villages participated actively. The main crops of the participants are Paddy, Citrus (Bathai/Sweet Orange), Cotton, Chilli and Vegetables.
Arrangements: At the venue, arrangements of Tent, 50 Chairs, Table, MFL Standee and Bannar of Reform Utsav 2026 - Kisan Sangosthi PM PRANAM were made. Handouts and leaflets regarding sustainable agriculture were distributed. Cool drinks, Biscuits and Water bottles were provided to all 40 farmers.
Subject Matter Covered: During the Sangosthi, detailed deliberation was made on PM PRANAM scheme and the key reforms and initiatives of the Government of India relevant to farmers and agriculture sector. Farmers were explained about the importance of 100% Neem Coating of Urea for paddy crop, use of new generation Nano Fertilizers and Potash Derived from Molasses (PDM) which reduces cost and improves quality of Citrus fruits. The concept of Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras as one stop solution for all agri-inputs and the implementation of One Nation One Fertilizer under Bharat Brand to ensure uniform quality was discussed. Special focus was given on PM-PRANAM to promote organic and bio-fertilizers for restoration of soil health in paddy fields. Farmers were also informed about the Drone Didi initiative for drone based fertilizer application which saves time and labour, Green Ammonia initiatives, reforms in iFMS and DBT for transparent subsidy transfer, integration of iFMS with AgriStack for digital farmer services, and the New Investment Policy for Urea to make India self-reliant in urea production. The progressive farmers shared their experiences in paddy and citrus cultivation.
Compliance: As per Office Memorandum of Department of Fertilizers and letter dated 30.09.2026 of HURL as coordinator, the Category-1 activity under Reform Utsav 2026 was mandatorily conducted in an organized and meaningful manner on Day-2 i.e. 06-10-2026. Daily activity data has been updated in the HURL shared sheet Kisan http://Sangosthi-2026.xlsx.by RO Hydrabad
S. Karuppaiah Manager Marketing, Telangana State MFL, RO-Hyderabad

NSO appeals for public cooperation in Socio-Economic Surveys across Assam
articles.full_content:
The Field Operations Division (FOD) of the National Statistics Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, is conducting large-scale socio-economic surveys across selected locations in Assam.
The surveys are aimed at collecting primary data on a wide range of socio-economic indicators, including household income, migration, debt and investment, employment, agriculture and industries.
The Regional Office, Guwahati, and the Sub-Regional Office, Silchar, will undertake the survey work at various locations during October 2026 under the districts Dhubri, Bajali, Baksa, Barpeta, Bongaigaon Chirang, Goalpara, Kamrup (R) , Kokrajhar, Nalbari, South Salmara Mankachar, Tamulpur, Kachar, Doma Hasao, Karbi Anglong and West Karbi Anglong. As part of the survey process, field officials will visit selected households and establishments to collect information us her here e ing scientifically designed survey schedules.
Appealing for public support, the Director and Regional Head, NSO (FOD), Regional Office, Guwahati, has requested citizens to extend full cooperation to the authorised officers and officials during the survey period by providing accurate and complete information. Such cooperation will help to generate reliable official statistics that are crucial for informed policy formulation and nation building.
The NSO has assured that all information collected during the surveys will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for statistical purposes.
The tentative schedule of visits by officials of the NSO (FOD) for conducting surveys during October 2026 is available here .

articles.title: PM Vishwakarma Awareness Programme on Branding and Marketing Held in Thoubal
articles.full_content:
A One-Day Awareness Programme on Branding and Marketing under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme (FY 2026–27) was organized by the MSME Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Imphal, on 06 October 2026 (Tuesday) at the Training Hall, Waikhom Mani Girls’ College, Thoubal, Manipur. The programme brought together around 150 PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries representing various traditional trades, along with key stakeholders, to strengthen awareness on branding, marketing, entrepreneurship, financial literacy and institutional support.
Shri M. Siva Sai Reddy, IEDS, Assistant Director, Programme Coordinator and In-charge, PM Vishwakarma Scheme, MSME-DFO, Imphal , presented an overview of the status and progress of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and highlighted key initiatives undertaken under the Scheme. He also elaborated on its various components and the support available to artisans for strengthening their skills, enterprises and livelihoods.
The inaugural session was graced by Smt. Yumnam Robita, IAS, Deputy Commissioner, Thoubal District, as the Chief Guest. In her address, she emphasized the importance of preserving traditional crafts while embracing innovation, entrepreneurship, branding and market-oriented approaches to enhance the income and livelihoods of traditional artisans.
Shri Oinam Deben Singh, General Manager, District Industries Centre (DIC), Thoubal , also addressed the participants and highlighted the importance of institutional support in promoting and strengthening local enterprises. Dr. Sorokhaibam Shyamkiran Singh, Vice Principal and SPOC, Waikhom Mani Girls’ College, highlighted the importance of skilling and capacity building in enhancing employment and entrepreneurial opportunities for youth. He also highlighted the college’s role as a Skill Hub in supporting skill development and capacity-building initiatives.
The programme featured a series of technical sessions aimed at enhancing the entrepreneurial capabilities and market readiness of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries. Shri Ngangom Birajit Singh, Lead District Manager (LDM), conducted a session on financial literacy, credit linkages and institutional support, providing beneficiaries with information on available financial services and credit facilities.
Shri Laishram Monoranjan Singh, Chief Executive Officer, KB PHILANTHROPY-5 , delivered a session on productivity enhancement through skill development, market trends and sales strategies . Shri Jiban Khundrakpam, Branding Consultant, Manipro Branding Solutions , conducted a session on entrepreneurship development, export opportunities, branding, packaging and product design , with emphasis on improving the marketability and competitiveness of traditional products.
